before: ‘A hundred measures of olive oil,' he answered. ‘Take your bill,' said the manager, ‘sit down quickly, and write fifty.'
verse: Then he asked another, ‘And how much do you owe?' ‘A hundred measures of wheat,' he replied. ‘Take your bill and write eighty,' he told him.
after: The master commended the dishonest manager because he had acted shrewdly. For the sons of this age are more shrewd in dealing with their own kind than are the sons of light.

before: Then the old prophet instructed his sons, “Saddle the donkey for me.” So they saddled it,

after: So the old prophet lifted up the body of the man of God, laid it on the donkey, and brought it back to his own city to mourn for him and bury him.

before: And: “I will be a Father to you, and you will be My sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty.”
verse: Therefore, beloved, since we have these promises, let us cleanse ourselves from everything that defiles body and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.
after: Make room for us in your hearts. We have wronged no one, we have corrupted no one, we have exploited no one.

before: Consequently, whoever resists authority is opposing what God has set in place, and those who do so will bring judgment on themselves.
verse: For rulers are not a terror to good conduct, but to bad. Do you want to be unafraid of the one in authority? Then do what is right, and you will have his approval.
after: For he is God's servant for your good. But if you do wrong, be afraid, for he does not carry the sword in vain. He is God's servant, an agent of retribution to the wrongdoer.

before: Understand, then, that it is not because of your righteousness that the LORD your God is giving you this good land to possess, for you are a stiff-necked people.
verse: Remember this, and never forget how you provoked the LORD your God in the wilderness. From the day you left the land of Egypt until you reached this place, you have been rebelling against the LORD.
after: At Horeb you provoked the LORD, and He was angry enough to destroy you.

before: “I have no husband,” the woman replied. Jesus said to her, “You are correct to say that you have no husband.
verse: In fact, you have had five husbands, and the man you now have is not your husband. You have spoken truthfully.”
after: “Sir,” the woman said, “I see that You are a prophet.

before: I will send fire on Magog and on those who dwell securely in the coastlands, and they will know that I am the LORD.
verse: So I will make My holy name known among My people Israel and will no longer allow it to be profaned. Then the nations will know that I am the LORD, the Holy One in Israel.
after: Yes, it is coming, and it will surely happen, declares the Lord GOD. This is the day of which I have spoken.

before: For this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: “The Daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time it is trampled. In just a little while her harvest time will come.”
verse: “Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has devoured me; he has crushed me. He has set me aside like an empty vessel; he has swallowed me like a monster; he filled his belly with my delicacies and vomited me out.
after: May the violence done to me and to my flesh be upon Babylon,” says the dweller of Zion. “May my blood be on the dwellers of Chaldea,” says Jerusalem.

before: Therefore this is what the LORD of Hosts says: ‘Because you have not obeyed My words,
verse: behold, I will summon all the families of the north, declares the LORD, and I will send for My servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, whom I will bring against this land, against its residents, and against all the surrounding nations. So I will devote them to destruction and make them an object of horror and contempt, an everlasting desolation.
after: Moreover, I will banish from them the sounds of joy and gladness, the voices of the bride and bridegroom, the sound of the millstones, and the light of the lamp.

before: and so that you may live long in the land that the LORD swore to your fathers to give them and their descendants, a land flowing with milk and honey.
verse: For the land that you are entering to possess is not like the land of Egypt, from which you have come, where you sowed your seed and irrigated on foot, like a vegetable garden.
after: But the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess is a land of mountains and valleys that drinks in the rain from heaven.

before: Then the LORD said to Gideon, “There are still too many men. Take them down to the water, and I will sift them for you there. If I say to you, ‘This one shall go with you,' he shall go. But if I say, ‘This one shall not go with you,' he shall not go.”
verse: So Gideon brought the men down to the water, and the LORD said to him, “Separate those who lap the water with their tongues like a dog from those who kneel to drink.”
after: And the number of those who lapped the water with their hands to their mouths was three hundred men; all the others knelt to drink.

before: So Moses and Aaron said to all the Israelites, “This evening you will know that it was the LORD who brought you out of the land of Egypt,
verse: and in the morning you will see the LORD's glory, because He has heard your grumbling against Him. For who are we, that you should grumble against us?”
after: And Moses added, “The LORD will give you meat to eat this evening and bread to fill you in the morning, for He has heard your grumbling against Him. Who are we? Your grumblings are not against us but against the LORD.”

before: because it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
verse: Therefore, when Christ came into the world, He said: “Sacrifice and offering You did not desire, but a body You prepared for Me.
after: In burnt offerings and sin offerings You took no delight.

before: During the reign of David there was a famine for three successive years, and David sought the face of the LORD. And the LORD said, “It is because of the blood shed by Saul and his family, because he killed the Gibeonites.”
verse: At this, David summoned the Gibeonites and spoke to them. (Now the Gibeonites were not Israelites, but a remnant of the Amorites. The Israelites had taken an oath concerning them, but in his zeal for Israel and Judah, Saul had sought to kill them.)
after: So David asked the Gibeonites, “What shall I do for you? How can I make amends so that you may bless the inheritance of the LORD?”

before: At that time Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to be baptized by John.
verse: But John tried to prevent Him, saying, “I need to be baptized by You, and do You come to me?”
after: “Let it be so now,” Jesus replied. “It is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness in this way.” Then John permitted Him.

before: We cared so deeply that we were delighted to share with you not only the gospel of God, but our own lives as well. That is how beloved you have become to us.
verse: Surely you recall, brothers, our labor and toil. We worked night and day so that we would not be a burden to anyone while we proclaimed to you the gospel of God.
after: You are witnesses, and so is God, of how holy, righteous, and blameless our conduct was among you who believed.

before: For He Himself is our peace, who has made the two one and has torn down the dividing wall of hostility
verse: by abolishing in His flesh the law of commandments and decrees. He did this to create in Himself one new man out of the two, thus making peace
after: and reconciling both of them to God in one body through the cross, by which He put to death their hostility.

before: Their father Jacob said to them, “You have deprived me of my sons. Joseph is gone and Simeon is no more. Now you want to take Benjamin. Everything is going against me!”
verse: Then Reuben said to his father, “You may kill my two sons if I fail to bring him back to you. Put him in my care, and I will return him.”
after: But Jacob replied, “My son will not go down there with you, for his brother is dead, and he alone is left. If any harm comes to him on your journey, you will bring my gray hair down to Sheol in sorrow.”

before: But the crowds found out and followed Him. He welcomed them and spoke to them about the kingdom of God, and He healed those who needed healing.
verse: As the day neared its end, the Twelve came to Jesus and said, “Dismiss the crowd so they can go to the surrounding villages and countryside for lodging and provisions. For we are in a desolate place here.”
after: But Jesus told them, “You give them something to eat.” “We have only five loaves of bread and two fish,” they answered, “unless we go and buy food for all these people.”

before: But whoever denies Me before men, I will also deny him before My Father in heaven.
verse: Do not assume that I have come to bring peace to the earth; I have not come to bring peace, but a sword.
after: For I have come to turn ‘a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.

before: The frogs will come up on you and your people and all your officials.'”
verse: And the LORD said to Moses, “Tell Aaron, ‘Stretch out your hand with your staff over the rivers and canals and ponds, and cause the frogs to come up onto the land of Egypt.'”
after: So Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt.

before: Unleash the fury of your wrath; look on every proud man and bring him low.
verse: Look on every proud man and humble him; trample the wicked where they stand.
after: Bury them together in the dust; imprison them in the grave.

before: They brought them to the magistrates and said, “These men are Jews and are throwing our city into turmoil
verse: by promoting customs that are unlawful for us Romans to adopt or practice.”
after: The crowd joined in the attack against Paul and Silas, and the magistrates ordered that they be stripped and beaten with rods.

before: As Peter continued to reflect on the vision, the Spirit said to him, “Behold, three men are looking for you.
verse: So get up! Go downstairs and accompany them without hesitation, because I have sent them.”
after: So Peter went down to the men and said, “Here am I, the one you are looking for. Why have you come?”

before: Then he washed his face and came back out. Regaining his composure, he said, “Serve the meal.”
verse: They separately served Joseph, his brothers, and the Egyptians. They ate separately because the Egyptians would not eat with the Hebrews, since that was detestable to them.
after: They were seated before Joseph in order by age, from the firstborn to the youngest, and the men looked at one another in astonishment.

before: And this day will be a memorial for you, and you are to celebrate it as a feast to the LORD, as a permanent statute for the generations to come.
verse: For seven days you must eat unleavened bread. On the first day you are to remove the leaven from your houses. Whoever eats anything leavened from the first day through the seventh must be cut off from Israel.
after: On the first day you are to hold a sacred assembly, and another on the seventh day. You must not do any work on those days, except to prepare the meals-that is all you may do.

before: Because of them, all the exiles of Judah who are in Babylon will use this curse: ‘May the LORD make you like Zedekiah and Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire!'
verse: For they have committed an outrage in Israel by committing adultery with the wives of their neighbors and speaking lies in My name, which I did not command them to do. I am He who knows, and I am a witness, declares the LORD.”
after: You are to tell Shemaiah the Nehelamite that

before: therefore you will no longer devour men or deprive your nation of its children, declares the Lord GOD.
verse: I will no longer allow the taunts of the nations to be heard against you, and you will no longer endure the reproach of the peoples or cause your nation to stumble, declares the Lord GOD.”
after: Again the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

before: A Psalm of David. Ascribe to the LORD, O heavenly beings, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.
verse: Ascribe to the LORD the glory due His name; worship the LORD in the splendor of His holiness.
after: The voice of the LORD is over the waters; the God of glory thunders; the LORD is heard over many waters.

before: But as for me, my feet had almost stumbled; my steps had nearly slipped.
verse: For I envied the arrogant when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.
after: They have no struggle in their death; their bodies are well-fed.

before: Which is easier: to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, ‘Get up and walk'?
verse: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins...” Then He said to the paralytic, “Get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”
after: And the man got up and went home.

before: “What guilt offering should we send back to Him?” asked the Philistines. “Five gold tumors and five gold rats,” they said, “according to the number of rulers of the Philistines, since the same plague has struck both you and your rulers.
verse: Make images of your tumors and of the rats that are ravaging the land. Give glory to the God of Israel, and perhaps He will lift His hand from you and your gods and your land.
after: Why harden your hearts as the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened theirs? When He afflicted them, did they not send the people out so they could go on their way?

before: So Joseph imprisoned them for three days,
verse: and on the third day he said to them, “I fear God. So do this and you will live:
after: If you are honest, leave one of your brothers in custody while the rest of you go and take back grain to relieve the hunger of your households.

before: Now therefore you are under a curse and will perpetually serve as woodcutters and water carriers for the house of my God.”
verse: The Gibeonites answered, “Your servants were told clearly that the LORD your God had commanded His servant Moses to give you all the land and wipe out all its inhabitants before you. So we greatly feared for our lives because of you, and that is why we have done this.
after: Now we are in your hands. Do to us whatever seems good and right to you.”

before: He will yet fill your mouth with laughter, and your lips with a shout of joy.
verse: Your enemies will be clothed in shame, and the tent of the wicked will be no more.”
after: Then Job answered:

before: Again I looked, and I considered all the oppression taking place under the sun. I saw the tears of the oppressed, and they had no comforter; the power lay in the hands of their oppressors, and there was no comforter.
verse: So I admired the dead, who had already died, above the living, who are still alive.
after: But better than both is he who has not yet existed, who has not seen the evil that is done under the sun.

before: The Levites did as Moses commanded, and that day about three thousand of the people fell dead.
verse: Afterward, Moses said, “Today you have been ordained for service to the LORD, since each man went against his son and his brother; so the LORD has bestowed a blessing on you this day.”
after: The next day Moses said to the people, “You have committed a great sin. Now I will go up to the LORD; perhaps I can make atonement for your sin.”

before: And do not neglect the Levite within your gates, since he has no portion or inheritance among you.
verse: At the end of every three years, bring a tenth of all your produce for that year and lay it up within your gates.
after: Then the Levite (because he has no portion or inheritance among you), the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow within your gates may come and eat and be satisfied. And the LORD your God will bless you in all the work of your hands.

before: Make a horn on each of its four corners, so that the horns are of one piece, and overlay it with bronze.
verse: Make all its utensils of bronze-its pots for removing ashes, its shovels, its sprinkling bowls, its meat forks, and its firepans.
after: Construct for it a grate of bronze mesh, and make a bronze ring at each of the four corners of the mesh.

before: Because you did not obey the LORD or carry out His burning anger against Amalek, the LORD has done this to you today.
verse: Moreover, the LORD will deliver Israel with you into the hand of the Philistines, and tomorrow you and your sons will be with me. And the LORD will deliver the army of Israel into the hand of the Philistines.”
after: Immediately Saul fell flat on the ground, terrified by the words of Samuel. And his strength was gone, because he had not eaten anything all that day and night.
